news.title: CAF Strategy Conference: Ouahbi – the youth developer who carried Morocco’s new generation to another World Cup quarter-final
news.lede: Mohamed Ouahbi will arrive at the CAF Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde with one of the clearest examples of how long-term investment in youth development can feed directly into success at senior international level. The 49-year-old was appointed Morocco coach only three months before the FIFA World Cup 2026, replacing Walid Regragui after the Atlas Lions had already established themselves among the leading sides in world football. Despite the limited preparation time, Ouahbi guided Morocco through the group stage and into the quarter-finals, where their campaign ended with a 2-0 defeat by France. In doing so, Morocco became the first African nation to reach the last eight at consecutive World Cups.

news.title: Nigeria's Special Eagles prep for 2026 Amputee World Cup
news.lede: Nigeria amputee football team training. Picture: Marabou News Agency. Nigeria's men's national amputee football team, known as the Special Eagles, is hard at work in Abuja as they prepare for the 2026 Amputee World Cup. The Major tournament will take place in San Juan De Los Lagos, Mexico, running from November 13 to 22.

news.title: Zidane says 'no regrets' over World Cup headbutt as France prepare to meet Italy
news.lede: Ahead of France's Nations League game against Italy on Friday, France football boss Zinedine Zidane insisted he had no regrets about headbutting Italy defender Marco Materazzi during the 2006 World Cup final – although he added that he was not proud of his actions. "The images always remind me of it," said Zidane. "They’re shown over and over again. But luckily that’s not all I ever did and there are other images that are nicer.”

news.title: Marquinhos: India Friendly A Golden Opportunity For Brazil's New Cycle
news.lede: Brazil's star centre-back Marquinhos shares insights into the Selecao's highly anticipated FIFA international friendly against India, emphasising its role in their post-World Cup rebuilding efforts and acknowledging the passionate Indian fan base. Brazil star centre-back Marquinhos is well aware of the Selecao's huge following in India and described their FIFA international friendly against the Blue Tigers a "golden opportunity" to gain valuable experience before embarking on a new cycle. The five-time world champions face India, ranked 138th in the world, in a much-anticipated friendly in Kolkata on Saturday. Yet to win the global showpiece since 2002, Brazil are looking to rebuild after their disappointing 2026 World Cup campaign.

news.title: Brazil Coach Carlo Ancelotti Discusses India Match, Team Building, And World Cup Aspirations
news.lede: Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti expressed respect for the Indian team ahead of their match in Kolkata, viewing it as an opportunity for his squad rather than a test. He discussed the challenges of managing a national team, the importance of commitment and joy in football, and the ongoing preparations for the 2026 World Cup, including significant squad changes and the blend of youth and experience. Ancelotti also reflected on Brazil's recent World Cup disappointment and the evolving nature of football.
